label: grants-probe-n1
_why:
ONE DETERMINISTIC QUESTION: ARE THE SUBJECT TECH GRANTS NEEDED AT ALL? (planned 2026-08-17, to run after anchorage-netseed-n1.)

User ruling: they are not, because a seeded port belongs to the OVERLORD's government rather than to the state's own country. That contradicts what I inferred earlier — that the engine gates `create_building` on the state's own country holding the technology — but that inference was drawn when the ports were CONVERSIONS of a locally-owned anchorage. They are now CREATED with explicit overlord government ownership, which is a different object, so the earlier finding may simply not carry. This probe settles it.

THE TEST IS THE 1836 BOOT DUMP AND NOTHING ELSE. The `building_inventory` metric fires at 1836.1.8, eight in-game days in, so the run needs about four minutes of wall clock. One arm suffices: the WITH-GRANTS answer is already measured — anchorage-netseed-n1 shows all 40 `building_port_steam` stubs present — so this run only has to answer whether they survive WITHOUT the fourteen subject grants.

READ: (a) the count of `building_port_steam` at the 1836.1.8 boot dump. **40 = the grants are unnecessary and get deleted.** Fewer, and the grants are load-bearing: name which states lost theirs, because that also identifies exactly which countries genuinely need one. (b) as a control that nothing else moved, `building_shipyard_metal` 3, `building_steel_mill` 15, `building_motor_industry` 11 and the anchorages still present beside the stubs.

⚠⚠ THE SECOND QUESTION — DID THE GRANTS CAUSE THE OWNER-LINK FLOOD? — IS DELIBERATELY NOT TESTED HERE, AND THE REASON IS THAT IT CANNOT BE, CHEAPLY. In anchorage-netseed-n1 all 18,723 errors fall in ELEVEN MONTHS, 1842.2 to 1843.1, bracketing the East India Company's war with the Khalsa Raj (play 1842.3.4, WARSTART 1842.6.12); BIC is one of the granted countries. But WARS ARE HIGHLY STOCHASTIC (user, 2026-08-17): of the wars not already running at 1836.1.1, only the Mexican-American and the Opium wars are at all reliable, so a BIC/Khalsa war in the 1840s cannot be counted on. A probe that waits for it would read zero in both arms on most seeds and prove nothing — and an earlier draft of THIS file ran only to 1841, which is before the errors even began, so it would have produced a confident null that meant nothing at all.

SO Q2 IS ANSWERED THE CHEAP WAY: if Q1 says the grants are unnecessary they are deleted, and their culpability becomes moot. If a later century run STILL floods with no grants present, the war gate in `emit_research_events.mjs` is the culprit and is investigated on its own terms. If Q1 says the grants are needed, then and only then does Q2 need a deliberate design — most likely a scripted war rather than a hoped-for one.

_comparison: anchorage-netseed-n1 (20260817_155024) is the WITH-GRANTS arm, already measured: 40 port_steam / 6 shipyard_metal / 15 steel_mill / 11 motor_industry at its 1836.1.8 boot dump, anchorages retained beside the stubs.
_caveats: ⚠⚠ VERIFY THE BOOT DUMP IS COMPLETE BEFORE READING IT. The first attempt (20260817_184413) ran only to 1837 and captured 3,411 BINV lines across 161 countries against the century run's 12,676 across 285 - about 27% - because the game self-quits moments after the ~12k-line boot burst and the log mirror has not drained it. Read that way it showed 19 of 40 stubs and would have concluded the grants are load-bearing, which is the OPPOSITE of what the complete dump may say. The span is now 1840 so the mirror has minutes to catch up. ALWAYS compare 0 and the distinct-country count against the reference run before drawing any conclusion from a boot dump. ⚠ The whole answer is in the 1836.1.8 boot dump; the run continues to 1837 only so the harness has a clean self-quit rather than a watchdog kill. ⚠ Do not read anything else from this run — one year is far too short for any economic reading, and it carries no wide sweep. ⚠ L19: check no orphaned victoria3.exe before launching; a live game from a previous batch makes the next run fail in about 20 seconds with a single-line log and a misleading `SCHEDULE DONE`.
